correctness.rationale: For n>=5, BB^T=(n-2)I+J and A=J+I-B^T B yield exact orthogonal sectors of dimensions 1,n-1,N-n. On these, K=(1-b)I+(a-b)A+bJ has eigenvalues positive on the constants and second harmonics, with the first-harmonic eigenvalue F=1-(n-3)e^-t+(n-4)e^(-2^p t). Its derivative has a strictly increasing bracket, proving one negative interval and one positive crossing exactly when (n-4)2^p>n-3. At a positive root the derivative is positive; differentiating in the power yields strict monotonicity. The critical-window equation e^t=1+m(1-e^-ct/m) has strictly increasing RHS in m and converges to 1+ct; a uniform Taylor expansion around the positive simple root gives the claimed positive first correction. Exact incidence identities and finite independent full-kernel checks passed using the included script; finite testing alone is not used to justify general quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The strongest closely related source, Aalipour et al. (arxiv:1509.01196, Theorems 3.9–3.10), supplies Johnson/Kneser eigenspaces and the raw distance spectrum, so those ingredients are expressly not claimed as new. Meckes (arxiv:1012.5863, Theorem 3.3) and Feragen et al. (arxiv:1411.0296) provide all-bandwidth positive-definiteness theory. The inspected materials and indexed mathematical records do not state the unique finite-bandwidth kernel threshold with full inertia and the nontrivial universal c-window with first finite-size correction. Algebraic accessibility and possible unindexed equivalent derivations remain risks.

value.rationale: Kernel positive definiteness at an individual bandwidth is the precise admissibility test for finite Gram/kernel methods and is strictly finer than negative type (the all-bandwidth criterion). This family offers an exact sharp transition from an n-1 dimensional negative space, through a singular Gram matrix, to strict positivity; the critical window captures the shrinking power threshold while the nonzero bandwidth converges to the universal exp(T)=1+cT law. The strictly increasing n-law and quantified correction make the result a structural all-size classification rather than a small-graph constant or a routine restatement of a known matrix spectrum.
